claim: Intrinsic load is set by the number of elements that must be held and related at once, not by the amount of material. Vocabulary lists are large but low in interactivity.
agent_test: Label items by interacting-element count; check whether error tracks count when item length is held fixed.

claim: Formal basis: complexity of a step is the number of variables related in parallel (relational complexity); capacity is a soft limit near four, and tasks above it need segmentation or conceptual chunking.
agent_test: Segment vs chunk ablation on high-arity items at equal tokens.

claim: Element-interactivity effect: split-attention, redundancy and modality effects show with high-interactivity material and shrink or vanish with low. Human evidence is from few small studies, mostly by one school (Sweller and colleagues).
agent_test: Add helper context to low vs high interactivity items; expect harm or no gain only on high.

claim: Leahy 2003 Exp 1 (N=48): audio+diagram beat text+diagram only on 8-element questions (34.3 vs 15.7 percent), no difference on 1-element ones. Per-question counts are uneven (7-element questions showed no gap).
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as design caution that effects are not smooth in the count.

claim: Expertise reversal and prior knowledge: the same material has fewer interacting elements for experts, so guidance helps novices and hurts experts (meta-analysis d=0.505 and -0.428, second-hand, not opened).
agent_test: Scale scaffold depth to a gate that estimates the agent's own familiarity with the item type.

claim: Intrinsic load is not fixed by element count alone: content type, ontological category and Hanoi variants with equal move counts differ in difficulty; and splitting or sequencing changes the effective load.
agent_test: Compare count-based difficulty prediction against a plain length predictor on mixed items.

claim: Self-report measurement of intrinsic load is weak: one-item ratings have no stable meaning, post hoc reading makes the theory hard to falsify, and ratings are order-biased (first unit drives the overall rating).
agent_test: Use performance-based difficulty (item response) not self-rated load when calibrating S0.

claim: In LLMs, accuracy falls as the number of interacting entities and rules rises, holding length and distractors fixed (CogniLoad: 12 of 22 models below 50 percent by d=5; gpt-5 0.82 and o3 0.80 at d=10).
agent_test: Replicate with our own puzzle generator; plot accuracy vs d for plain vs decomposed arm at equal tokens.

claim: In LLMs, accuracy falls with relational complexity when entity count and input size are fixed (45 percent drop RC 3 to 9; 93 percent fall RC 5 to 20 on phylogeny). RC 1-2 stays near perfect even at 30x30. More thinking tokens and best-of-N did not fix high RC.
agent_test: Test whether decomposition that lowers RC per step beats extra tokens at equal budget.

claim: Adding clauses or interacting quantities to grade-school math lowers accuracy and raises variance (Gemma2-9b-it 84.4 / 79.1 / 68.1 / 41.8 across M1, Symbolic, P1, P2); irrelevant clauses cause drops up to 65 percent.
agent_test: Insert NoOp clauses into our items; measure whether a relevance filter step recovers accuracy.

claim: Tool-use difficulty follows a dependency-graph load; accuracy falls with load for every model, and a function-calling fine-tune resisted it best.
agent_test: Compute a dependency-edge load for our tasks; check it predicts failure.

claim: Explicit load-aware decomposition can cut tokens about 35 percent at equal accuracy (Llama-3-70B GSM8K 92.5 at 485 tokens vs 92.3 at 310; MATH 53.9 at 812 vs 53.5 at 525). Single author, no ablation of the load-assessment step.
agent_test: Ablate: load estimate + decompose vs decompose alone vs CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Splitting a high-load task across specialised agents helps reasoning-heavy tasks and hurts low-load instruction following; agent count is non-monotonic and gains are modest.
agent_test: Gate decomposition on estimated load; show gating beats always-decompose.

claim: Least-to-most decomposition gives large gains where the split is clean and sub-steps are easy (SCAN length 99.7 vs CoT 16.2; last-letter length 12: 74.0 vs 31.8), with hand-written exemplars.
agent_test: Test model-written decomposition vs hand-written on real tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Complexity collapse: accuracy goes near zero past a model-specific size on puzzles, but part of the Hanoi collapse is an output-length and unsolvable-instance artefact; solution length is confounded with interactivity. Gap search: stepwise chunked output still fails near 8 disks (Gemini), and standard Hanoi is saturated while flat-to-flat (joint state) is not, so the collapse is partly format and partly state maintenance.
agent_test: Ask for a procedure or function, not an enumerated move list, for long-output items.

claim: Compositional tasks fail by error propagation across the computation graph (82.3 percent of correct 4x2-digit answers had a wrong node); evidence is from 2023 models.
agent_test: Check step-level verification at each decomposed node on current models.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Counting interacting elements is analyst-assigned (Chen 2016 gave about 6 vs 1 by author judgement; REL and CogniLoad assign by design), with no second-rater validation.
agent_test: Have two independent raters (or models) count elements on 30 items; check agreement.

claim: Working-memory-style limits in LLMs are partly task-understanding failures (n-back): capacity claims should be treated as unproven.
agent_test: Control for task-set maintenance before attributing failure to a capacity limit.

claim: Gating decomposition on estimated load beats always- and never-decomposing: the closest measured case is failure-gated as-needed decomposition (ADaPT: TextCraft 52.0 vs ReAct 19.0 vs plan-and-execute 27.0; ALFWorld 71.6 vs 43.3 vs 43.3). The gate is a failure signal, tokens are not matched, models are 2023, and a pre-solve load estimate has not been tested.
agent_test: On our items, compare never, always and load-gated decomposition at equal total tokens; find the break-even load.

claim: Extra context costs more when intrinsic load is high, the same direction as the human interaction: distractor damage grows with step count for CoT (GSM-IC; flat for least-to-most), and the CogniLoad distractor trough widens with intrinsic difficulty d. Context length alone also hurts with perfect retrieval and masked filler (13.9 to 85 percent). The claim that extra context hurts only low-load items is not supported.
agent_test: Vary distractor count at two load levels on our tasks and check for the interaction.

claim: The CogniLoad U-shaped distractor curve is real but weak for current frontier models: gpt-5 0.97/0.89/0.91 and o3 0.93/0.89/0.88 across low/mid/high needle ratio, trough strongest at d = 5 and N = 20 and gone by N = 250. No mechanism is given; the generator may confound it with effective chain length (my reading, untested).
agent_test: Re-run a small ratio sweep with a fixed number of relevant updates to test the confound.

claim: Self-estimates of load carry some signal but depend on how they are elicited: self-rated effort or ability predicts the model's own failures (AUROC up to 0.83 to 0.89, +6.7 to +10.1 points over confidence; 12 models, 38 tasks), while asking how hard an item is for humans gives weak alignment (rho below 0.50) and near-chance self-error prediction in most models.
agent_test: Elicit effort before solving and measure AUROC against failure on our own items.

claim: No study was found that compares a rater-made element count with length, steps or depth for predicting LLM failure on the same items. Indirect support: a structure-based bandwidth measure predicts failure independent of length (BAPO), and LLM raters track human item difficulty at rho about 0.5 to 0.8 depending on method. Inter-rater agreement for element counts remains untested.
agent_test: Have two raters and one model count elements on 100 items; compare predictive power with length and steps by logistic regression.

claim: Part of the benefit of splitting comes from separating contexts, not only from shorter chains: independent sub-problems solved in one context need up to 10 to 20 times more generations than the product of separate runs (Llama-3-8B), and 5 to 10 times for four-problem compositions with Llama-3-70B. Lower per-step arity inside a step is still not separated from this.
agent_test: Ablate: same sub-steps in one context, in separate contexts, and with arity-reduced steps, at equal tokens.

claim: Scaffolds have a measured cost where they are not needed: CoT gains concentrate in symbolic, math and logic tasks (+14.2, +12.3, +6.9) and are about 0.7 points elsewhere; CoT lowers accuracy by up to 23 points (GPT-4o) on implicit-pattern tasks; R1 is reported to do worse with few-shot examples. This is an expertise-reversal analogue at model level, but not tested at equal tokens within one model across item difficulty.
agent_test: Per model class, measure scaffold-on vs scaffold-off accuracy by load bin at equal tokens.

claim: Chunking the output (ask for the next p moves) or asking for a procedure helps Hanoi, but there is no evidence outside Hanoi that a procedure format restores scaling; a function works only when a compact rule exists.
agent_test: Test procedure-vs-enumeration on two non-Hanoi tasks with and without a compact rule.

claim: Whether intrinsic load can be changed by sequencing is unsettled for LLMs: ordering demonstrations by difficulty gave +9 percent F1 on instruction-tuned models (ICCL) but only about +0.2 to +0.5 points in a step-count-ordering ablation on Llama3-8B. A restructure that shortens state (recite then solve) gave up to +31.2 points on GSM8K for Mistral-7B at long length. None of these isolates elements first within one problem.
agent_test: Compare plain decomposition with isolated-elements-first sequencing at equal tokens on our tasks.

claim: The best k (interacting elements per part) differs by model and was not found measured for splitting. CogniLoad ID50 (max interacting entities/attributes at 50 percent accuracy under mean length) ranges from below 0 (small reasoning models) to 19.07 (DS-R1-0528), but it bundles entities and attributes and is not a k.
schema_part: O3 decompose (split until at most k)
agent_test: Measure ID50-style thresholds on our own tasks per model class, then split to that k.
